published_statement: Abstract: 'extends to a wider class of spacetimes previous results of Geroch and Tipler that show that topology change is only to be had at a price ... The interpolating spacetime is required to obey a condition called causal compactness, a condition satisfied in a very wide range of situations ... topology change is kinematically possible ... Geroch's closed-universe argument is applied to causally compact spacetimes to show that even in this wider class of spacetimes there are causality violations associated with topology change ... in dimensions >= 3 causally compact topology-changing spacetimes cannot satisfy Einstein's equation (with a reasonable source) ... it makes no assumptions about geodesic completeness; i.e., it does not permit topology change even at the price of singularities (of the standard incomplete-geodesic variety).' THEOREM 1 (Sec. IV): 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' THEOREM 3 (Sec. V): '(time-oriented) causally compact interpolating spacetime of dimension >= 3 ... i) every full null geodesic has a point at which F_abcd = U_[a R_b]ef[c U_d] U^e U^f != 0 ... ii) ... the half-integral null convergence condition holds ... Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.' SEC. IX: 'Neither Geroch's original theorem, nor its mild generalization in section IV, assume anything about the energy-momentum tensor, or indeed about a field equation'; 'If the standard incomplete-geodesic definition is used ... as long as the causal compactness condition is met, causality violations have to occur when the topology changes, even if incomplete geodesics are admitted. But, other definitions of a singularity may make the statement true'; 'A popular modification ... is to abandon the Lorentzian framework altogether and to use a Euclidean path integral formalism. But even within the general Lorentzian framework there are still several interesting possibilities': A] dropping causal compactness (Tipler Thm 5, closed-universe case, 'under some mild additional assumptions', gives a singularity or a point at infinity, 'a highly undesirable feature'); B] weakening the curvature constraints ('would not affect the presence of causality violations'; either alter Einstein's equation, which 'would have to be fairly severe', OR 'violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated', as in wormhole-creation discussions); C] degenerate metrics (Sorkin, Ashtekar, Horowitz: 'even in standard general relativity (couched in first-order language) Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed. So, this might well prove to be the correct approach').
published_hypotheses: M is an interpolating spacetime: connected smooth (C^infinity; C^3 manifold with C^2 fields suffices, Sec. VIII) Hausdorff paracompact n-manifold with boundary S1 u S2 u T, T empty or a compact timelike tube diffeomorphic to dS1 x [0,1] (Sec. II.A)
a smooth NON-DEGENERATE Lorentz metric everywhere on M, S1 and S2 spacelike; S1 initial (nothing to its past), S2 final (Sec. II.A)
time-oriented (Thm 1, Thm 3) -- removable for non-empty boundaries (Sec. VII: a CTC-free causally compact interpolant is then time-orientable)
causal compactness: I(p) compact for every p in M (Sec. III.B); for open universes, M is the causally compact region of an externally simple spacetime (Sec. III.E)

differentiability of the timelike vector field V^a (C^1 for unique integral curves): 'If we were satisfied with metrics that are only continuous ... S1 and S2 need not be diffeomorphic, even if causality violations are forbidden' (Sec. VIII)
Theorem 1 assumes NOTHING about T_ab or a field equation (Sec. IX)

Theorem 3 only: dimension >= 3; (i) null generic condition on every full null geodesic; (ii) half-integral null convergence condition to the past along past-complete null geodesics -- implied, via Einstein's equation (any Lambda), by T_ab V^a V^b >= K for all unit timelike V (Sec. VI); no geodesic-completeness assumption
'singularity' means the standard incomplete-geodesic definition; other definitions may change the conclusion (Sec. IX)

Tipler Thm 5 (IX.A): closed-universe case, non-compact interpolant, 'mild additional assumptions'; that a SINGULARITY (not a point at infinity) occurs needs 'the significant additional assumption that there is an upper bound on the lengths of certain timelike curves'

later_literature.ref: arXiv:2505.02210 (Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou 2025, v4 Apr 2026), 'Wormhole Nucleation via Topological Surgery in Lorentzian Geometry'
later_literature.what: An explicit wormhole nucleation built from a Morse 0-surgery. Its naked singularity is removed by the Misner connected sum with CP^2, and the result is an everywhere non-degenerate Lorentzian metric in which 'the singularity is replaced by a region containing closed timelike curves'. It violates all standard energy conditions, and its conclusions are 'purely kinematic'. This is Borde's Theorem 1 price realised in the tree's own case (creating a throat), and it is the paper formation.py reads.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:2202.09833v4 (Garcia-Heveling 2022/2024), 'Topology change with Morse functions: progress on the Borde-Sorkin conjecture'
later_literature.what: Develops route IX.C, the one the tree omits. Metrics that vanish at isolated Morse points give topology change without CTCs (Geroch's CTC applies to non-degenerate compact cobordisms; 'the only way to have topology change without time travel is by allowing the spacetime metric to degenerate'). It proves a special case of the Borde-Sorkin conjecture (causal continuity iff no index 1 or n-1 points), argues the original conjecture is false, and proposes refined Conjecture 3. It also notes non-compact slices allow topology change without CTCs and without singular points (Sanchez, NAMED-NOT-READ), which agrees with the tree's H_closed scoping.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:gr-qc/9711070 (Dowker & Surya 1998), 'Topology Change and Causal Continuity'
later_literature.what: With Morse (degenerate) metrics, 'no topological cobordism is excluded'. In 3+1 dimensions, if the Borde-Sorkin conjecture holds, every transition is achievable by a causally continuous cobordism with only index-2 points (Lickorish-Wallace). The S^3 -> S^2 x S^1 wormhole transition admits an index-2 (causally continuous) route, while the 'natural' two-regions-touch route has index 1 and is causally discontinuous. This is conditional on a conjecture, and quantum-field behaviour on such backgrounds is Sorkin's separate, open conjecture.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. Borde 1994 uses no measured datum: Theorem 1 is purely kinematical and assumes nothing about T_ab or a field equation, and Theorem 3 uses Einstein's equation with energy-condition hypotheses. No later measurement can move it, and no numerical input has moved (data_at_publication). The evidence that something was incomplete concerns the scope of the framework, not a datum. (1) Borde already knew and named the routes outside his hypotheses: C^0 metrics (Sec. VIII), degenerate metrics (IX.C), energy-condition violation against Theorem 3 (IX.B) and the Euclidean path integral. The tree's use, not the source, drops IX.C and the IX.B sub-route. (2) What came later is mathematics: the causal theory of degenerate Morse metrics (Borde-Dowker-Garcia-Sorkin-Surya 1999, cited in 2202.09833; Dowker-Surya 1998; Garcia-Heveling 2022-24) and an explicit non-singular nucleation (2505.02210). The first develops the omitted route. It shows topology change without CTCs at the price of isolated metric degeneracies, conditional in 3+1 on a conjecture now argued false in its original form and refined. The second confirms that the CTC price is paid when the metric is kept non-degenerate. (3) Later quantum-energy-inequality and ANEC work bears on Theorem 3's hypothesis (ii) but was not read in this stage and is not relied on. Conclusion, evidence either way: no lacked datum changes Theorem 1 or Theorem 3 on their stated hypotheses. The later work shows the tree's 'ALL THREE ... LEAVE GR OR ACCEPT A PATHOLOGY' rests on a route list shorter than Borde's own. Whether a degenerate point counts as a 'pathology' (Borde: 'these kinds of singularities'; Garcia-Heveling: points 'where nothing special happens') is a definitional choice this audit does not make.
grade_evidence: The theorem the tree leans on STANDS as published. Every quotation is verbatim (C1: 8/8), and the finite and closed-form steps re-derive (C3-C8: Lorentz-from-vector-field, the null-direction quartic, focusing, the energy-condition limit, the Euler arithmetic, finite shadows of Thms 1-2). No datum enters or has moved. The tree's USE is narrower than the source in three ways, each shown here. (a) The smooth non-degenerate Lorentz metric hypothesis is dropped: H_cc and the GEROCH-BORDE encoding (specthm.py:615-616, 1838-1844) carry causal compactness alone, and z3 (C9) shows the encoding is not implied by Theorem 1 without it. (b) 'ALL THREE' escapes (create.py:78, 211-221, 349; specthm.py:1781-1783) omits Borde's IX.C degenerate-metric route, which Borde places within the general Lorentzian framework and calls possibly 'the correct approach'. It also omits IX.B's within-Einstein-equation energy-condition sub-route (C2: 4 routes against 3). any_escape_stays_in_lorentzian_gr() = False is therefore established only for the tree's three. (c) 'section VIII.A' (specthm.py:587, 1850) should be IX.A, a citation discrepancy. None of this refutes the tree's operative conclusion: under causal compactness with a smooth non-degenerate metric and the standard singularity definition, creating a throat forces a CTC in the interpolating region whatever the matter, and 2505.02210 realises exactly that. Not WRONG: no counterexample to anything Borde states. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum. Not plain STANDS: two hypotheses and one route are dropped, which is NARROWED's definition.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree adds the smooth, non-degenerate (C^1-or-better) Lorentz metric to H_cc and GEROCH-BORDE; lists IX.C (degenerate metrics) and IX.B's energy-condition sub-route among Borde's routes, with IX.C's status in Lorentzian GR marked OPEN rather than False; and corrects 'VIII.A' to 'IX.A'. To WRONG for the tree's use (not for Borde): a demonstration, inside the tree's own definitions, that a degenerate-metric creation counts as staying in Lorentzian GR without a pathology would falsify any_escape_stays_in_lorentzian_gr() = False as a statement about Borde's routes. That is a definitional ruling for M, not a computation. For Borde's own result: only a counterexample to Theorem 1 or 3 on their stated hypotheses, and none is known in the literature read.
